rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Pheretima (earthworm) is a model annelid: a segmented worm with ~100–150 metameres, a clitellum (segments 15–31) for cocoon formation, and setae on each segment for peristaltic locomotion. It has a true coelom with septa, circular and longitudinal muscles, and breathes through its moist skin. Earthworms are hermaphrodites that cross-fertilise.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Earthworm body: prostomium + 100–150 segments + clitellum (segments 15–31) + setae
Coelom: true body cavity, fluid-filled, divided by septa
Respiration: cutaneous (through moist skin)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Earthworms are Annelids, NOT arthropods; they have a soft body with setae, not a hard exoskeleton.  ·  The clitellum is a thickened, saddle-like region used to form the cocoon — it is NOT a reproductive organ itself.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a labelled external diagram of Pheretima (prostomium, clitellum, setae).  ·  The clitellum segments (15–31 in Pheretima) are a common exam detail.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Pheretima posthuma — the Indian earthworm model; clitellum on segments 15–31.  ·  Lumbricus terrestris — the European garden worm; used in many textbooks.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Earthworms have a closed circulatory system (blood vessels + heart-like vessels), not an open one.  ·  Respiration is through the moist skin (cutaneous); there are no gills or lungs.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label external Pheretima  ·  Explain clitellum role

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Earthworm = Annelid = segmented + coelom + setae.  ·  Clitellum = saddle + cocoon (segments 15–31).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Describe the external anatomy of Pheretima.  ·  Explain the body plan of the earthworm (coelom, septa, muscle layers).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Annelid body plan  ·  Segments (metameres)  ·  Clitellum  ·  Setae

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Pheretima: annelid, ~10–15 cm, ~100–150 segments.  ·  Clitellum (segments 15–31): saddle-like; forms the cocoon.  ·  Setae on each segment: bristles for anchoring in peristaltic movement.  ·  Body plan: coelom (true body cavity), circular + longitudinal muscles, septa.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Earthworms contain ~100–150 segments (metameres).  ·  A single gram of soil can contain several earthworms; they turn over a significant fraction of topsoil each year.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: How does the earthworm benefit the soil?  ·  State the taxonomic position of Pheretima.  ·  Explain the role of setae in earthworm locomotion.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Describe the role of the clitellum and setae.  ·  Explain soil benefits of earthworms.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: The setae (bristles) on each segment provide grip during peristaltic locomotion.  ·  The clitellum (segments 15–31) secretes the cocoon that encloses the eggs.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Pheretima posthuma (earthworm): annelid (segmented worm); ~10–15 cm long; ~100–150 segments.  ·  External features: clitellum (segments 15–31 in Pheretima) for reproduction; setae (bristles) on each segment for anchoring; chaetae; prostomium (first segment, sensory).  ·  Body wall: cuticle + circular and longitudinal muscles; coelom (true body cavity) with coelomic fluid; septa between segments.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Coelom and septa  ·  Cutaneous respiration  ·  Hermaphroditism

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Soil benefits  ·  Cutaneous respiration through moist skin; night-active; lives in moist soil.  ·  Hermaphrodite (both sexes); cross-fertilisation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Soil benefit: aeration, humus, structure, fertility.  ·  Earthworms are hermaphrodites (both male and female organs) but exchange sperm with another worm (cross-fertilisation).  ·  Segments are called "metameres"; each has a set of setae for anchoring during locomotion.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Cutaneous respiration and peristaltic locomotion are key functions.  ·  Soil benefits (aeration, humus, structure) are a favourite application question.  ·  Memorise the clitellum segments (15–31 in Pheretima).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Learn the external features (prostomium, clitellum, setae).  ·  Explain peristaltic locomotion using setae.  ·  State the soil benefits of earthworms.
